Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

joinpoint 0.1.0

First version.

Models

  • joinpoint() fits joinpoint regression models to one or more series (cohorts given by by): linear or log-linear models of rates, age adjusted rates, proportions, percents, counts or other values, with constant variance, supplied standard errors, Poisson variance, first order autocorrelated errors or a supplied covariance matrix.
  • Joinpoints are found by an exhaustive grid search with placement constraints and optional points between observations (Lerman 1980), compiled in C++ and evaluated from cross products.
  • Poisson and logistic joinpoint models fitted by exact maximum likelihood (Czajkowski et al. 2008), with Wald intervals, profile deviance joinpoint intervals, deviance based criteria and optional quasi-likelihood dispersion.
  • Continuous joinpoints between observations by an exact search (Hudson 1966).
  • Covariates (covariates = ~ ...), excluded data points, shifted x values, jump and comparability ratio models for coding changes (Chen et al. 2020).

Model selection

  • WBIC, BIC, BIC3, modified BIC, data dependent selection, the sequential permutation test (Kim et al. 2000) and a sequential Monte Carlo likelihood ratio test, with optional early stopping (Besag and Clifford 1991) and a minimum APC difference worth detecting.
  • A time budget lowers the recommended maximum number of joinpoints when the exhaustive search would be too slow.

Inference

  • APC, AAPC (full range, last N observations, custom ranges) and joinpoint location estimates with parametric or empirical quantile confidence intervals and p values (Kim et al. 2017).
  • Pairwise tests of parallelism and coincidence with AAPC comparisons and multiplicity adjustment (jp_compare(); Kim et al. 2004).
  • Clustering of contiguous age groups (jp_cluster()) and direct age adjustment with delay factors (age_adjust()).

Output and graphics

  • Accessors apc(), aapc(), joinpoints(), model_selection(), model_estimates(), jump_estimates(), the publication table jp_table(), coef(), vcov(), fitted(), residuals(), predict() and as.data.frame() methods, and jp_export() for delimited text files.
  • ggplot2 graphics: autoplot() trend figures with segment labels placed to avoid each other and the curves, plot_apc(), plot_aapc(), plot_models(), plot_selection(), plot_residuals(), comparison plots, theme_joinpoint() and color scales.

Data and documentation

  • Data sets us_mortality, std_populations and ontario_bmi.
  • Eight vignettes, including a reproduction of a published analysis of prepregnancy body mass index (Khademioore et al. 2026).
